North Dakota: what's on the November 3, 2026 ballot

Every candidate below is listed alphabetically, with party shown as text only. Open a name for their stated positions, background and recent news, each with sources.

Open North Dakota on the map

Key dates

  • Early in-person voting: October 19, 2026 to November 2, 2026. Each county sets its own early voting dates and locations, and not every county offers it. These dates are the widest window state law allows. Check with your county auditor.
  • Last day to apply for an absentee ballot: November 2, 2026. Absentee ballots became available 2026-09-24. Your county must receive the voted ballot by the time polls close on Election Day.
  • Election Day: November 3, 2026. Polls open between 7 a.m. and 9 a.m. depending on location and close at 7 p.m. local time.

Official election information: North Dakota Secretary of State – Elections (vote.nd.gov)

Ballot measures

Constitutional Measure No. 1 – 60% vote to approve constitutional amendments

Referred by the Legislature (HCR 3003). Proposed amendments to the North Dakota Constitution, whether referred by the Legislature or started by citizen petition, would need at least 60% of the vote to pass. It amends Article III, Section 9 and Article IV, Section 16.

Yes: A yes vote means future constitutional amendments would need at least 60% voter approval to take effect.
No: A no vote means constitutional amendments would still pass with a simple majority of votes.

Initiated Constitutional Measure No. 2 – Free school breakfast and lunch

Placed on the ballot by citizen petition. Public school districts, public schools and public charter schools would have to give enrolled students one breakfast and one lunch each school day at no cost. Nonpublic and tribal schools could choose to take part. The state would reimburse schools at 100% of current free-meal rates, adjusted for inflation, paid from the Legacy Earnings Fund if the Legislature does not name another funding source. The Secretary of State's analysis estimates the cost at $124.3 million to $134.3 million for the 2027–2029 biennium.

Yes: A yes vote adds a section to the state constitution requiring free school breakfast and lunch for public school students, with state reimbursement to schools.
No: A no vote leaves the constitution unchanged, so free school meals would not be required by the constitution.
